scientific_question: Can a small curriculum of independently verifiable Python tasks, selected near the current Qwen3.5-4B policy's learnability frontier and optimized with group-relative executable reward, produce a reproducible behavioral improvement over the exact unchanged base?

hypotheses.H0: A bounded executable-reward RL intervention does not produce a meaningful paired improvement over the exact unchanged Qwen3.5-4B base on a frozen disjoint development set.
hypotheses.H1: A bounded executable-reward RL intervention on frontier-selected independently verified tasks produces a meaningful paired improvement over the exact unchanged base without unacceptable regressions.

v0_scope.hardware_target: single RTX 4070 Ti SUPER-class 16 GiB GPU

non_goals: treating Qwen3.8-27B answers as gold student targets
using protected benchmarks for RL reward training
asynchronous rollout complexity before synchronous causality is established
hard_stop_rules: No PVRL model-training conclusion before FTR-G1 is satisfied.
Stop if hidden grader state is readable or writable by the solver.
Stop if harness failures are converted into candidate failures.
Stop if Qwen3.5 multi-turn token-prefix continuity is violated.
Stop if rollout/log-prob/loss-mask alignment is ambiguous.
Stop if protected benchmark contamination is detected.
Stop if checkpoint/resume identity is ambiguous.

reference_architecture.paper: FrogNano: Training a 4B Coding Agent via Online Task Synthesis
reference_architecture.adaptation_note: PVRL adopts executable environments, frontier calibration, and behavioral RL while deliberately simplifying to synchronous short-context QLoRA experiments on local hardware.
